##  · DOC1-init-open — DOC1-init: manifest device names, blame table, bucket sizing, restart connections

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 5

Decision references: docs/servers/init.md#the-boot-manifest, docs/servers/init.md#restarts-and-reboots, docs/servers/wire.md#a-launcher-releases-its-childs-grants, docs/beyond/image-cache.md

Evidence: docs/servers/init.md states NAME/NAME-irq, buckets=N, restarts with new connections and blame; wire.md: a child's grants never outlive its launcher; image cache in docs/beyond/image-cache.md. Code departures are todo pages consoled-irq-name and server-bucket-counts, placed in M1.

### Servers writer (2) · Question

Event: `e3224217252a0d451dfb7fb1762065e6` · 2026-09-26T08:16:00Z

> DOC1 servers/init.md carries these in Open: until answered. (1) Device naming: a UART or disk is two objects (MMIO region + interrupt). Recommend: two manifest entries and two named handles, NAME and NAME-irq, under the manifest name rule (no ':'). (2) Blame message init->steward has no table. Recommend: one typed call in a `steward` table, `blame(account: u64, labels: bytes)`, reply `-`, written with the steward page. (3) Servers with compiled-in bucket counts (bootfsd 16, consoled 4, keyd 16; ipd takes buckets=N): recommend every shared server takes `buckets=N` as an argument so the manifest sizes it (serving.md residual: an undersized server is a channel). (4) A restarted server: same startup block and the same fresh connections, or new ones? Recommend new fresh connections (the old server's minted table is gone, R27). (5) Image copy per child vs shared read-only cache: recommend keep the copy for M1, record the cache as a later question. (6) wire.md: when a launcher itself dies, who releases its children's grants? Recommend its own launcher's disconnect_all at each server, no new server-side exit tracking.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `950284a38e658ccfc48399b23928d0b4` · 2026-09-26T08:16:59Z

> Architect ruling, servers/init.md, M1 (separation and containment). All six are decided: (1) amended, (2) and (3) sharpened, (4) to (6) adopted. Every Open on the page closes except the bundle-pages question, which boot.md owns.
> 
> (1) AMENDED: ONE manifest entry per device, TWO named handles. A `devices` entry names a device-tree node, and init hands that node's objects together to the one server that holds the entry: NAME for the register region and NAME-irq for the interrupt (whichever exist). Two separate entries would let a manifest split one device between two holders. The holder of the interrupt could then mask or acknowledge the other's device and time its activity. One entry also keeps R34's (confined placement) 'one device object' check whole. Name rule addition: a device name may not end in '-irq' and is at most 60 bytes, so NAME-irq never collides and fits the 64-byte rule.
> 
> (2) ADOPTED, sharpened. One typed call in the `steward` table: blame(account: u64, labels: bytes, server: string), reply '-'. `server` is the faulting server's manifest name, for the audit record; the steward's rule counts by (account, label set) only. Two security properties the page must state:
> - Only init can blame. The call is accepted only through a root badge the steward gives init alone. Anyone who could send blame could have another principal's sessions ended, by forging three crashes.
> - A wedged steward cannot stall restarts. init restarts the server first, then blames, with a timeout. A blame lost to a timeout is reported on the console, and the page states it as a residual.
> 
> (3) ADOPTED, sharpened. Every shared server takes `buckets=N`, parsed once in the serving library (libs/rt), not per server, and none has a compiled-in count. init checks at boot that N is at least the number of distinct (account, label set)s the manifest routes to that server, plus its system callers, and refuses the boot otherwise. That makes R26's (admission fairness) 'never binds in normal use' checkable instead of hoped for. Sizing when users are added at run time is M5 (persist, install, share): the steward's job, Open there, not here.
> 
> (4) ADOPTED. A restarted server gets new fresh connections: the same manifest names, arguments and receive endpoint, but a new startup block. When the server exited, init as its launcher disconnected the dead instance's connections (the releasing-grants rule), then minted new ones for the new instance. The server's own table starts empty with a newly drawn first badge (R27 (badge allocation)).
> 
> (5) ADOPTED: keep the copy in M1 and after. A shared read-only image cache mapped into several principals' processes is a cross-principal cache-timing surface. It was deferred with the shared content-addressed store for exactly that covert-channel reason (legacy PACKAGES, Later). Record it in beyond/, not as an Open.
> 
> (6) ADOPTED, and it needs no new mechanism. Minted::disconnect already frees a capability and everything minted under it. A child's connections were minted through its launcher's, so when the launcher's own launcher disconnects the dead launcher's connections, every descendant's connections go with them. Rule text for wire.md: "A child's grants never outlive its launcher's: disconnecting a launcher's connection releases every connection minted under it, at every depth. Servers track no exits." An orphaned child keeps running in its budget, if that budget lives, but loses its server connections. That fails closed, and the page says so.
> 
> TESTS for M1:
> - a manifest splitting a device, or naming one ending in -irq, is refused;
> - blame from any badge but init's is refused;
> - an undersized buckets=N refuses the boot;
> - a restarted server's old connection ids are dead;
> - killing a launcher leaves its orphan's connections dead at every server.

### Architect · Progress

Event: `29e7764e0cd41b7b2fefae7a77eae0e1` · 2026-09-26T08:16:59Z

> cc: DOC1-init-open answered; all six are decided.
> (1) One devices entry per node yields NAME and NAME-irq for the same holder, so a device cannot be split; names are at most 60 bytes and none ends in -irq.
> (2) steward blame(account, labels, server), accepted only through init's root badge (forged blame would be a cross-principal DoS). init restarts first and blames with a timeout.
> (3) buckets=N for every shared server, parsed once in libs/rt; init refuses the boot if N is below the manifest's routed (account, label set)s.
> (4) A restart gets new fresh connections.
> (5) The copy stays; a shared image cache goes to beyond/ (a covert channel).
> (6) Recursive disconnect already covers orphans; wire.md states it and no new tracking is needed.
